articleTitle: Designing the Power Oscillation Damping Controller for a Non-Inertial Renewable Driven Energy Source by Using a Non-Rigid Infinite Bus Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Over the past decade, there has been a substantial increase in renewable energy-based generation to fulfill global energy demands and reduce carbon emissions. To integrate a large number of renewable energy sources (RESs) to the electric grid, the conventional synchronous generators needed to be replaced. As a result, future power systems are likely to have reduced natural inertia and damping, leading to stability issues such as angular instability and low-frequency oscillations (LFO). Undamped LFO can impose considerable stress on the power transmission capabilities of the grid. Therefore, it becomes crucial to equip the RES with a well-designed power oscillation damper. This paper proposes a novel system frequency response-based non-rigid infinite bus modeling framework to design a power oscillation damping controller for inverter-based non-inertial RESs. The effectiveness of the proposed oscillation damping controller design is evaluated using non-linear time domain analyses. These analyses are conducted on the WSCC 9-bus 3-machine system, simulated on the MATLAB/Simulink platform.

articleTitle: Renewable Energy Sizing for Electric Vehicle Charging: A Case Study of Karnataka, India
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: India, like many other nations, is going through the transitional phase of electrifying its transport sector. As a member of the EV30@30 campaign led by the International Energy Agency (IEA), India aims to achieve a 30% sales share for electric vehicles (EVs) by 2030. The state of Karnataka is a leader in the nation’s clean energy transition and is currently at the third position in EV sales among all states. However, an accelerated transition to zero-emission vehicles will eventually put the state’s power grid under acute stress, as it tries to meet the additional power demand from EV charging. Our study aimed to assess the impact of this shift by estimating the number of EVs that will ply on the roads of Karnataka by financial year (FY) 2029-30 and forecasting the energy required for charging these EVs. Further, acknowledging that a truly green transport requires that renewable energy (RE) sources be used to charge EVs (instead of fossil-fuel-based ones), the study includes a generation planning analysis wherein the amount of RE generation capacity required to meet the projected state demand (including the demand from EV charging) with least generation cost is estimated for FY 2029-30. The findings emphasise the importance of optimsing the energy mix (keeping the least-cost RE source availability in mind), and integrating energy storage systems into the grid for decarbonisation while ensuring a reliable and affordable power supply.

articleTitle: Real-Time Energy Data Extraction and Analysis of a Nanogrid System in BVRIT Campus for Critical Loads Using IoT Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: This paper presents a real-time method for extracting and analyzing energy data from a nanogrid system at the BVRIT campus using Internet of Things devices. The nanogrid system aims to store solar energy in batteries during the day and power critical AC loads at night. It includes six LED lamps, a street light, and a ceiling fan. The Nanogrid system comprises two 12 V, 150 Ah batteries, a 24 V, 1500 VA, 1200 W inverter, and a timer switch activating loads at 6 PM and deactivating them at 5 AM. Two IoT modules, each with Pzem004T & ESP8266 NodeMCU, monitor energy flow from the solar PV to the battery and from the battery to the AC loads. The real-time energy data analysis was done for three loading conditions with one-minute data extraction intervals. The battery efficiency was also calculated for all the three different loading conditions. An efficiency of 51.72% and 51.90% was obtained for loading conditions 1 and 3; for loading condition 2, the efficiency was found to be 43.22%, which implies that variation in loading condition impacts the battery efficiency.

articleTitle: Conformance testing tool for Power SCADA Communication Protocol
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Conformance test of products and attestation for standard compliance gives confidence to end users that product is implemented as per the protocol standard. Conformance testing plays a critical role in guaranteeing interoperability within Power Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems. This work presents the development of a dedicated conformance testing tool for the IEC 60870-5-104 communication protocol, widely used in the power industry. By leveraging this tool, developers and users can verify that their IEC 608705-104 implementations strictly adhere to the standard, minimizing the risk of compatibility issues during system integration. The testing methodology aligns with the IEC 60870-5-604 standard, ensuring a comprehensive evaluation of the protocol’s functionality and conformance. This work also discusses the conformance testing procedure with relevant examples, highlighting its significance in ensuring reliable and efficient testing environment.

articleTitle: Low-Frequency and Small-Signal Aggregate Load Model Estimation using Ambient Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Load modeling is a challenging problem even today due to the diverse, time-varying and complex nature of loads. The paper investigates the use of the well-known ARMAX method for obtaining a low-frequency, small-signal, aggregate, and dynamic load model using ambient measurements. A realistic model of a 16-machine system driven by random low-level load switching is used to analyze the accuracy of this method. The paper highlights the limitations of the method and the conditions under which it is suitable for identifying the load models. It is shown that the influence of the local load switching noise on the local bus voltage and frequency is a critical factor for accurate estimation. The method works well only if this feedback or the level of local load switching noise is low. An indicator to flag the estimates that are likely to be unreliable is proposed and validated.

articleTitle: Fault Location for Series Compensated Lines Eliminating Parameters as a Setting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Unlike protection applications, precise fault locator requires accurate line parameters which are not constant over the time as a result of aging and environmental impact on conductors. Traditional fault location approaches for series compensated lines are dependent on the prior knowledge of line electrical parameters, percentage and type of compensation. However, nonlinear characteristics of Metal Oxide Varistor (MOV) during fault makes the task of fault location more complex. In order to address these, a setting free fault location methodology for series compensated lines using synchronized data is proposed which is independent of MOV characteristics. The fault location algorithm is phasor-based and parameters are estimated using Dommel’s time domain equations. Estimation of parameters requires computation of propagation constant which is obtained using first two travelling wave peak arrival times of arial mode component of both end fault currents. Wavelet transform technique is used to extract the travelling waves. The proposed method is independent of the percentage, type, location of the compensation and MOV characteristics. The proposed method is verified using data simulated in PSCAD/EMTDC tools. The proposed method is tested for different fault scenarios and performance is found to be accurate.

articleTitle: Grounded Fault Type Identification in an Inverter Based Resources Network using Spherical Coordinate System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Uniqueness in behavior of renewable energy sources (RESs) based power generation with regard to fault signature when compared with usual synchronous generator (SG) based systems have put forward challenges in terms of protection. To differentiate single line-to-ground (LG) faults from double line-to-ground faults (LLG) robust identification of fault type is important. In this paper, an index designed on spherical coordinate system (SCS) is formulated. Cross-symmetrical power as a new identity is formulated. The proposed method is pivoted on symmetrical components and calculation of phasor for the fundamental component by using Fourier transformation. It is tested for its resilience against fault distance, fault resistance, fault inception angle (FIA) and series compensation.

articleTitle: Robust Control of Multiple Energy System that is Insensitive to the Power Forecast Error
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Multiple energy system (or called integrated energy system), including electricity, heat, cooling, and gas, has been emerging in some large or medium industrial parks because it could improve the energy efficiency. Conventional control technologies usually rely on the precise power forecast or abundant data to track the uncertainty of the renewable energy or the load, however these are not so available or economic in the real condition. This paper realized the algorithm of optimally distributing the energy flexibilities into different time sections of a day to cover the uncertainties, and the real-time control of the hardware to maintain the power balance. Typical hardware scenario was formulated for the evaluation of the technology. The result showed that, compared with the conventional technology, the new algorithm could reduce 1.3% energy cost and 2.6% CO2 emission when the renewable energy penetration ratio is 5%; and reduce 4.6% energy cost and 5.9% CO2 emission when the renewable energy penetration ratio is 45%.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Electricity Theft Detection using Extreme Gradient Boosting with Optuna Optimization in Smart Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Electricity theft poses significant challenges to power utilities, leading to considerable financial losses and operational inefficiencies. This study introduces an innovative approach combining Extreme Gradient Boosting (XG-Boost) with the Optuna optimization method (OOM) to improve electricity theft detection. XG-Boost is known for its speed and accuracy in handling large datasets, offering robust feature selection and powerful boosting capabilities. Optuna is an efficient hyperparameter tuning technique to optimize model performance. Experiments conducted on real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, with the proposed model surpassing conventional models in terms of Accuracy, F1, AUC, and Kappa Score. Furthermore, computational efficiency has also been considered a key parameter that further improves the practicality of the model. This study highlights the potential of integrating gradient boosting machines with optimization techniques to enhance electricity theft detection, thereby contributing to the reduction of non-technical losses and promoting the efficiency of smart power distribution systems.

articleTitle: Approximate Entropy based prevention of third zone distance relay maloperation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Third zone distance relays tend to maloperate during power swings, static load encroachment and voltage instability events. Even during voltage recovery events, there are chances of third zone distance relay maloperation. Prevention of distance relay maloperation during delayed voltage recovery events requires identification of vulnerability of distance relays with the existing method in literature. As long as the impedance trajectory is outside the third zone reach after fault clearance, the vulnerability can be found using relay margin. The third zone distance relay may malfunction, if the impedance trajectory remains inside the third zone reach even after fault clearance due to a delayed voltage recovery event. The approximate entropy based method is proposed to identify the fault occurrence and fault clearance events. The proposed method is applied to the distance relays of the 68 bus system, and it is observed from the results of the case studies that the distance relays do not maloperate during non-fault events and operate only during fault events.

articleTitle: Computational Aspects of Including the Stator and Network Transients in Stability Programs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: In power system stability (TS) programs, stator and network transients are neglected to reduce computational burden as the frequency of interest lies within 10 Hz. Network transients, particularly, cannot be ignored when inverter-based resources (IBR) are involved, as these require a broad frequency spectrum in simulations. This paper explores the computational of stability programs including stator and network transients for small and large systems. Two synchronous machine models, discrete domain and continuous domain voltage behind impedance dq0-machine models, for including machine and network transients are compared with the dq0-machine model used in TS programs. The system equations in state-space form are solved using trapezoidal method of integration with 1 ms step size. The discrete dq0-model is found to be better due to fewer network interface equations. A speed optimized C-program bench-marked with commercial EMTP software is used for simulations of WECC 9 Bus system, IEEE 118 Bus system, IEEE 300 Bus system, and Pegase 9241 Bus system. For smaller systems, execution times of models including transients are found to be comparable to TS programs. For large system, the actual time is only 102s for a 10s simulation on a standard desktop which is quite acceptable. Although the number of equations increase by 220%, the computational time only increases by 76% for large systems. The execution time can be reduced further using parallel processing.

articleTitle: Hybrid Machine Learning Models for Improved Short-Term Wind Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Wind's intermittent nature adds complexity to its analysis and its integration to electrical systems. So, accurate wind forecasting is crucial for effectively incorporating wind energy into power systems. This paper proposes an improved hybrid model for short-term wind prediction. It utilizes Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD), a data-driven de-noising technique, to break down signals into more interpretable components. EMD separates nonlinear non-stationary data into Intrinsic Mode Functions (IMF) and a residue, which are then input to a Convolutional Neural Network. EMD is prone to mode mixing issues, where a single IMF contains drastically different scales or a signal of a certain scale is spread across multiple IMFs, leading to signal intermittency. To address this, Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition (EEMD) is introduced, incorporating white noise ensembles to establish a consistent reference frame in the time-frequency domain. This added noise helps consolidate similar signal portions within a single IMF. The IMFs and residues obtained from EMD and EEMD are fed into a Convolutional Neural Network and compared with benchmark models such as Bi LSTM and LSTM. Performance evaluation of these Machine Learning Algorithms is done and compared with various performance metrics such as MSE, MAE, RMSE, MAPE, and Loss and testing time. The hybrid model exhibited superior performance over other machine learning models in enhanced wind speed forecasting.

articleTitle: Investigating the Impact of Induction Motor Starting on Grid-Forming Inverter-Based Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Microgrids using inverter-based resources (IBR) are becoming increasingly popular due to the sharp rise in energy consumption. With well-defined frequency and voltage droop control algorithms, these microgrids use parallel linked inverters that exchange power according to their ratings. With increased penetration of IBRs, stable islanded operation of a microgrid is aspired irrespective of the connected load. The induction motor starting either draws a high inrush current or currents with harmonic content. This current nature can interfere with the grid-forming (GFM) inverter control loops and create complications in the islanded microgrid. This paper considers different starting methods of induction motors connected to a GFM, and a comparison concerning starting current, voltage drop, frequency drop, and total harmonic distortion (THD) is carried out. The analysis is supported through simulations using MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Assessing the Economic Advantages of Integrating Bi-Directional EVSE into HEMS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: This paper assesses the economic advantage of bidirectional EVSE integration in Home Energy management System(HEMS) for energy import and export. A framework is proposed for this integration and this framework was tested on a typical home configuration. A comparative study for NEM 3.0 and dynamic tariffs was done by Incrementally adding Photovoltaic (PV) systems, Battery system, a uni-directional EVSE and a bi-directional EVSE into HEMS. This study utilizes publicly available data for these tariffs. This study presents positive results regarding economic advantages and the possibility of extending the framework to create optimized configurations for each homeowner based on their energy needs to maximize benefits.

Author Keywords: home energy management system (HEMS) and mixed integer linear programming (MILP)

articleTitle: Approximate Branch Flow Models for Three-Phase Unbalanced Network: A Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Optimal Power Flow (OPF) algorithms are crucial tools for Distribution Network Operators (DNOs) to ensure smooth system operation while transitioning to a decentralized, decarbonized, and digitized power grid. Within OPF algorithms, power flow equations that characterize three-phase distribution networks are essential but complex components. This paper evaluates the accuracy of three commonly used approximate models of the original branch flow-based three-phase power flow equations: the SOCP-based hybrid model, the linear model, and the approximated nonlinear model. Detailed formulations of these models are provided, including their underlying assumptions, approximations, and relaxations. These models are then tested on a 25-bus unbalanced distribution network, with their power flow results compared to those obtained from the standard backward forward sweep algorithm. A comprehensive comparative analysis is conducted, offering critical insights into the appropriate use of these models. This analysis aims to assist researchers in selecting the most suitable model for characterizing three-phase unbalanced distribution networks in their studies.

articleTitle: An Emission and Uncertainty Aware Optimal Dispatch of Multi-Energy Hub
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The integration of different energy carriers within a smart energy system with a significant presence of renewable energy sources (RES), such as wind energy conversion system (WECS), and solar photovoltaic (PV) system has made the energy hub (EH) a crucial component. The efficient management and coordination of EH's resources play a critical role in meeting kinds of energy demand at a minimal cost and achieving environmentally sustainable operation. In pursuit of these objectives, this study presents an economic-environmental EH framework that incorporates a substantial integration of RES. The EH comprises solar PV, WT, combined heat and power (CHP) unit, battery energy storage system (BESS), heat energy storage system (HESS), electric heat pump (EHP), electric boiler (EB), heat furnace (HF), absorption chiller (AC), and electric chiller (EC). The Monte-Carlo (MC) approach has been used to forecast the uncertainties (scenario generation) associated with RES, various types of energy consumption, electricity, and gas prices. The Kantorovich algorithm is employed for scenario reduction. The proposed framework is formulated as a multi-objective (MO) stochastic mixed-integer non-linear programming (MINLP) problem and solved using BARON solver in GAMS software. The simulation study validates the proposed model of EH.

articleTitle: Series Arc Fault Detection in DC Networks and Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Series arc fault (SAF) usually occurs due to damaged insulation, stretching/elongation of wires due to strain and hanging, poor line connections, poor joints, and lines damaged by pets, etc., This can cause serious hazards such as fires, explosions, and loss of assets. Considering the recent popularity of EVs, an SAF detection system must be installed to detect and protect the EVs from any such hazards. As a primitive work, this paper proposes an SAF detection method using the strength of high-frequency components that occur in the current signal during series arcing. When an SAF occurs, distinct abnormal electrical signals emerge characterized by elevated harmonics compared to normal working conditions. The proposed method underscores the efficacy of utilizing peak-to-peak features from normal and arcing conditions to differentiate between their respective current signals accurately, thus enhancing safety and mitigating potential hazards associated with DC networks and EVs.

articleTitle: An Experimental Evaluation of a Blockchain-based Peer-to-Peer Energy Trading Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Increasing penetration of Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) like solar PV, Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), electric vehicles and the digitization of power grids are turning consumers into prosumers. The excess energy generated by these prosumers can either be fed back into the grid or used for Peer-to-Peer (P2P) trading. P2P energy trading is a new paradigm that introduces flexibility among electricity users, where the energy from DERs is traded locally. This paper proposes an optimization model for P2P energy trading between prosumers and consumers such that the economic benefits of both groups are maximized by minimizing the total cost incurred in purchasing electricity. Further, it uses a blockchain-based platform for securing the transactions conducted during P2P energy trading. The proposed model’s effectiveness is tested on a test rig developed at IIT Gandhinagar, which consists of two peers. One of the peers acts like a prosumer with solar PV generation and BESS, whereas the other peer is a consumer. Results reveal that the proposed model provides better economic benefits to the prosumers than the feed-in tariff model.

articleTitle: Power System Optimization using an Adaptive Fuzzy Campus Placement based Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The use of optimization tools in complex problems is becoming increasingly crucial to overcome the challenging task of achieving efficient results. The Novel Adaptive Fuzzy Campus Placement based Optimization Algorithm (AFCPOA) is a new method for solving optimization problems that is based on campus recruiting process used in universities. In this study, two power system optimization problems, namely, Economic Load Dispatch (ELD) and Optimal Power Flow (OPF) have been tested on IEEE 30 bus test system. The main objective of ELD is scheduling generation units to lower costs while meeting system constraints, whereas OPF decides how to dispatch generating units to meet the demand for power at the lowest possible cost. The proposed method (AFCPOA) is applied on 16 Congress on Evolutionary Computation (CEC) benchmark test functions for validation and subsequently applied to two power system optimization problems ELD and OPF under MATLAB environment. The proposed AFCPOA method shows significant improvement in results compared with other methods for optimization problems.

Author Keywords: Adaptive Fuzzy Campus Placement based Optimization Algorithm (AFCPOA)

articleTitle: Source Identification and Analysis of very low frequency oscillation in Rajasthan Solar complex
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: To address global environmental concerns, countries across the globe are transitioning to low-carbon economies and decarbonizing their electricity sector. As one of the fastest-growing economies and the second-most populous country, India also embraces sustainable options to fulfil its energy needs and has set ambitious targets to achieve 50 percent of its installed generation capacity with renewables by 2030 and meet the Net Zero emissions target by 2070. This Energy Transition of India entails increasing presence of variable and intermittent Renewable Energy Sources like solar & wind in the energy mix. This presents a grid-level challenge for security & stability. Throughout the world one issue faced in grid operation with higher inverter-based resources penetration is low frequency oscillation.Oscillations with very low frequency at 0.1 Hz, have been observed in voltage and reactive power in practical solar photovoltaic systems when power exporting ramps up to a certain level. This paper provides an explanation on the formation of 0.1-Hz oscillations and identifies three critical factors that lead to the oscillations: communication delay between the plant-level control and the inverter-level control, high volt/var sensitivity at a high-power exporting level, and the volt-var feedback system consisting of the plant control, inverter control and the grid impact. Furthermore, a critical feature of the 0.1-Hz oscillation is also explained: why oscillations appear only in voltage and var, but not in real power. Also Impact of fault level on the control stability of slower outer control loop of solar plants.

articleTitle: Optimal Mobile Power Source Depot Placement for Resilient Coupled Power Transport Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Ensuring an uninterrupted power supply is crucial in today’s electricity-dependent world, where disruptions can cause severe economic crises and endanger lives. However, maintaining consistent power during natural disasters is challenging. Therefore, it is common practice to have small backup systems at load ends to support essential demands. This paper explores effective strategies for optimally placing a Mobile Power Source (MPS) depot within a realistic coupled power-transport network. The goal is to ensure the fastest possible service to backup systems located at all nodes within the network. An agent-based routing model is employed to determine the optimal routes for effective service provision during the restoration period of a disrupted network, whether due to a natural disaster or a cyber-attack. An iterative optimization algorithm, incorporating the agent-based optimal route model, is used to identify the best starting node for the depot. This approach ensures the most efficient service, minimizing downtime by meeting the power backup replenishment needs across the transportation network. Various case studies have been performed to validate the proposed algorithm on a real life coupled transport electric network of the the Indian Institute of Technology, Kanpur (IITK) campus area.

articleTitle: Collaborative Solutions for LVRT Integration, Auto-Reclose, and Distance Relaying Challenges for Type-3 Wind Power Plant connected Integrated Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: This paper explores challenges encountered in the integration of Type-3 wind and Inverter based solar power plants with the grid, focusing on protection issues in Extra High Voltage transmission lines. It investigates fault scenarios and proposes novel solutions to address them, emphasizing collaborative efforts across stakeholders. Key issues include non-operation of distance relays, delayed fault clearance, and auto-reclosure failures. The proposed solutions aim to enhance system stability, reduce mean time to restore (MTTR), and ensure compliance with Low Voltage Ride Through (LVRT) standards.

articleTitle: Model based Protection for Export Cables Connecting Off-shore Wind Farms to the Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Long export cables help in transfer of the electricity generated from offshore wind farms. Installation and maintenance of such cables are expensive. Reliable protection system which safeguards them during faults is essential. Limited fault currents, unique and non-homogeneous fault response from the wind farm converters, multiple inhomogeneous cable sections, etc. may render traditional protection principles such as distance and differential inadequate. This paper explores the application of an alternate principle, namely model based protection (MBP). It uses the model and measurements related to the export cable in a state estimation framework to detect faults. In addition to detection of faults, MBP can also help identify faulted phases and/or faulted cable section which can be beneficial for other fault management applications. MBP is comprehensive and can potentially minimize the need for complementary protection relays, thereby reducing the overall footprint of protection and control system in offshore platforms. Case studies are done using PSCAD/EMTDC simulations of a typical 220 kV, 160 km long export cable network connecting an offshore wind farm to the main grid.

articleTitle: Hardware Signature Extraction from an Intelligent Electronic Device
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Intelligent Electronic Devices (IED) perform various critical functions like protection and measurements in a power grid. It is essential to identify the IED with a unique signature to ensure the cyber security of the power grid. This paper presents a method to extract the hardware signature from a custom designed IED platform. The analog to digital converter (ADC) and Parallella processor of the IED platform are utilized to obtain the hardware signature. A finite state machine is developed in the Parallella processor to control the ADC to generate different data sets for signature extraction. Using the box and whisker statistical method, transients in the data set are removed and the signature extraction is performed. The proposed method utilizes only a hundred samples of 1kHz data to extract signatures. The long-term repeatability of the developed signature is tested by performing a large number of experiments. It is observed that the extracted signature is repeatable with an allowance for one bit flip. The proposed method is compared with an existing method, demonstrating its ability to generate signatures with fewer data samples.

articleTitle: Distributed Generation Curtailment for Maintaining Voltage Stability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The progressive integration of distributed generation (DG) gives rise to significant overgeneration within distribution networks. In some cases, it will lead to grid instability and voltage fluctuations, resulting in equipment damage or failures. The goal of this paper is to prevent several impacts of high integration of distributed generation, like grid instability and voltage stabilization challenges. There are several methods aimed at overcoming these impacts to preserve the stability of the network. This paper uses the power curtailment of distributed generation in a dynamic distribution network reconfiguration problem, obtaining a topology with optimized power losses. The novel feature is that only the amount of excess production violating the voltage limits is curtailed. A curtailment model and a relaxed voltage model are presented and can be used for industrial applications. They are tested on a small representative network and a modified IEEE-33 system.

articleTitle: Adaptive chaotic class topper optimization to solve Non-convex CHPED problems in power systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: This paper proposed a population-based meta-heuristic algorithm, an adaptive chaotic class topper optimization (AC-CTO) algorithm for solving combined heat and power economic dispatch (CHPED) problems. The proposed algorithm is an improved version of classical class topper optimization, where the desirable practical solutions are obtained based on the learning process, improving the students’ knowledge. Here, the complexity of combined heat and power is increased due to their mutual interdependence and is non-linear in nature. The main goal is to achieve the minimum fuel cost while satisfying demand, considering the practical system constraints such as valve-point effects, prohibited operating zones, and transmission loss. To evaluate the performance, the proposed algorithm is tested for two case studies, one without system losses – 4 unit system and the other with system losses – 7 unit system. The results of the study indicate that AC-CTO algorithms outperform popular optimization methods to solve the CHPED problems and obtain the lowest fuel cost.

Author Keywords: Combined Heat and Power Economic Dispatch (CHPED)

articleTitle: Improving EV Charging System Reliability by Detecting Aborting Causes using Algorithmic Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The increased prevalence of EV has given rise to an augmented demand for EV charging infrastructure. However, the dependability of charging systems can be compromised by various factors, including power grid complications, communication difficulties, issues with components, or EV and supply station incompatibility. This can result in charging interruptions, which can be an inconvenience for EV owners and could deter the adoption of EVs. In the context of advancing EV charging infrastructure, this research endeavors to pinpoint the pivotal parameters influencing the performance of the EV charging module. To achieve this objective, an experimental study is conducted, involving the collection of data in diverse scenarios. Subsequently, a comprehensive analysis is undertaken employing the RIPPER Algorithm to generate IF-THEN rules with sensitive and non-sensitive signals. Additionally, this study utilizes feature importance metrics to identify and present the top sensitive parameters, contributing to enhancing the understanding of critical factors in EV charging systems. This approach facilitates advancements in their reliability and efficiency.

articleTitle: Placement of Micro-PMUs and Voltage Estimation in Radial Distribution Networks with Zero Injection constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: This paper introduces a new method for optimizing the placement of Micro-Phasor Measurement Units (μPMUs) and improving voltage estimation in radial distribution networks, with a focus on Zero Injection Bus (ZIB) constraints. Radial networks, particularly those integrating increasing levels of distributed generation (DG), face significant challenges in state estimation. The proposed approach employs mathematical optimization to strategically place μPMUs, ensuring comprehensive network observability and accurate voltage estimation using Phasor Measurement Unit (PMU) technology and the Weighted Least Squares (WLS) algorithm, while effectively addressing the complexities posed by ZIBs. Comparative analyses with existing methods demonstrate that the proposed approach reduce μPMUs requirements for the IEEE 33-bus and IEEE 69-bus systems, achieving full observability with fewer units. Additionally, it supports high-quality voltage estimation, overcoming key limitations of prior methods. The results confirm the efficiency and practicality of the approach, offering a cost-effective solution for enhanced monitoring and control in modern distribution networks with renewable energy integration.

articleTitle: Detection of Transformer Circular Flow Effects
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: To calculate partial power flows of transformers, until now only phase-shifting transformers (PST) can be considered. In this work, the algorithm for the calculation of partial power flows is extended to all transformers. First of all, the PST, which are modeled so far by the help of phase-shifting distribution factors (PSDF), play a significant role for power flow controlling assets. In addition to these, however, any other transformer with longitudinal or longitudinal and angle regulation can also be considered as a driver of circular flows. In contrast to previously used methods such as PSDF or heuristic methods for placing PST, the principle shown here uses the current equation to calculate the influence of all transformers on other equipment. Every transformer is represented by a pair of current sources, which stand for the current driven by the regulation-driven voltage difference inside each transformer. The presented method is validated on a test grid with two voltage levels and five transformers.

articleTitle: Integration of Battery Energy Storage System into Distribution Networks: An Approach based on State-of-Health Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Battery energy storage systems (BESS) are essential for optimizing energy management in distribution networks. This paper presents a comprehensive framework and detailed mathematical model for integrating BESS into the distribution network to reduce the operating costs of a local distribution company (LDC). It proposes a state-of-health (SoH) estimation based on calendar aging for lithium-ion (Li-ion) batteries to be incorporated into the LDC planning strategy. This estimate accurately predicts the SoH of BESS over time and ensures more effective long-term planning and cost management. The results show that the proposed model provides accurate and reliable SoH estimates, which contributes to improving the efficiency and sustainability of on-grid energy storage systems.

articleTitle: Voltage Regulation in Distribution Network using Bi-Level Multi-Agent Optimal Energy Management
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: In this paper, a bi-level optimal energy management with a techno-economic objective of regulating the voltage and mitigating economic losses in a distribution network (DN) with 100% rooftop photovoltaic (PV) penetration is presented. A deep reinforcement learning (DRL) agent is used at the network level to achieve the techno-economic objectives of the distribution system operator (DSO). Within DN, each smart home with energy management system (HEMS) uses DRL for effective energy management when responding to the economic signal broadcasted by the DSO agent. Further two different methods of generating economic signals, i.e., dynamic price generation at different levels of HEMS penetration are studied. The results indicate that the proposed bi-level optimal energy management is effective in mitigating the undervoltage scenario using demand response at all levels of HEMS penetration. However, the effectiveness of the proposed system in regulating the overvoltage in the DN is observed only at 100% HEMS penetration.

articleTitle: Line-to-Ground Arc Flash Fault Detection Using Distance Protection Scheme for Wildfire
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The outbreak of wildfires due to undetected arc-flash faults poses serious safety hazards to the New Zealand power system and community, resulting in fatalities and infrastructure damage. The consequences of arc-flash faults are particularly significant in low-voltage (LV) distribution systems due to the relatively short overhead line lengths, high fault resistance, and low line-to-ground fault current. This paper explores a distance protection scheme using IEDs with a quadrilateral characteristic on an IEEE LV test feeder to leverage its separately settable resistance and reactance reach for superior arc-fault compensation. The proposed method is validated through analysis and simulations in the software environments of DIGSI 5, OMICRON Test Universe, and OpenDSS. Simulation outcomes indicate that the proposed scheme is feasible for the detection and prevention of wildfires.

articleTitle: Consumer enrollment in residential demand response: Implications across diverse societies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The transition of a conventional energy system to a sustainable one requires the availability of flexible loads on the consumption side. Coupling several individual residential consumers can provide a high degree of flexibility, which can help the energy system during times of need. This paper aims to analyze the potential enrollment of residential consumers in demand response across different societies by using an agent-based model. The motivators determining consumer enrollment are personal satisfaction, the neighborhood effect, and the social effect. In this paper, three different societies, in which all consumers have one major motivator fixed, are considered. A Monte Carlo analysis was performed to address the randomness associated with assigning different neighborhoods, friends, and expected annual savings of consumers. The highest enrollment rate was observed in April, and the lowest between June and September for the societies where consumers had personal satisfaction and the social effect as their major motivators. The society in which consumers were mainly motivated by the neighborhood effect was highly dependent on the random assignment of the neighborhood, and the enrollment rate was independent of the electricity prices, which, in turn, resulted in complete enrollment or disenrollment of the neighborhood in the society.

articleTitle: An Accurate Fault Location Method for Power Distribution System with Integration of Inverter Based Resources
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Existing fault location methods in electrical distribution network fails when it comes to mesh distribution network with integrated renewable energy sources. The extensive lateral branches and load points makes it more difficult to identify the exact location of the fault. This paper proposes a fault location solution based on fault passage indicator with minimal measurements to accurately identify the fault location in meshed distribution network with integrated renewable energy. The core idea is to develop a standardized user interface where users can upload distribution network details and fault data. The interface will then compute and display the exact fault location within the system and the same will be visualized on a mapping interface with QGIS (Quantum Geographic Information System)

articleTitle: Modeling Battery Degradation in Energy and Performance-Based Regulation Markets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The growing share of uncertain and variable power generation sources has led independent system operators (ISOs) to seek resources with fast ramp rates for frequency regulation. Recent improvements in battery energy storage systems (BESSs) have increased their use in ancillary service markets. The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission also made a provision for ISOs to facilitate the participation of BESSs in the clearing of energy and ancillary service markets by incorporating their physical and operational characteristics through Order No. 841. However, frequent BESS cycling causes degradation that results in decreased battery life. Thus, battery degradation should be incorporated into the usage pricing in different markets. This paper proposes a mathematical formulation to model the degradation cost of different battery technologies. Further, a market-clearing framework for the co-optimized energy and performance-based regulation markets is proposed. The effects and costs associated with battery degradation are considered in both energy and regulation scheduling. Suitable case studies comparing the effect of the degradation cost of different battery technologies in the proposed market-clearing framework are performed on the standard IEEE test system.

articleTitle: Estimation of flashovers in the EHV/UHV lines on east coast due to lightning produced by Bay of Bengal cyclones
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The modern world relies on continuous and reliable power. Lightning is one of the natural threats that can lead to, amongst others, power interruptions and damage to equipment. It is a threat even for EHV and UHV grids and forms the primary reason for outages. Cyclones can bring many lightning strikes to the electric grid within a few days. In addition to the above, it can affect the system's stability. The Bay of Bengal produces a considerable number of cyclones that affect the electric grid on the east coast. As such, there is no effort to quantify the consequential threat of lightning flashovers; hence, the present work was undertaken. The electro-geometric model (EGM), suggested by IEEE standards, assessed the normalized number of strokes to the phase conductor and intercepted by the tower/ground wire. The associated probabilities are also estimated for typical EHV and UHV lines. Lines are modeled in EMTP to assess the flashovers. The cyclones' trajectory, speed, and ground flash density are evaluated based on the literature. The possible number of flashovers in the EHV and UHV grid along the East Coast is accessed using the same. The maximum number of flashovers is also estimated for engineering purposes, which seems to range in thousands.

articleTitle: Voltage Control in Radial Distribution Systems using Deep Reinforcement Learning Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach for voltage control in radial power distribution systems using the state-of-the-art Double Deep Q-Network (DDQN) algorithm to optimize the operation of two capacitor banks within a 13-bus radial network under different load configurations. A Python-based framework facilitates interfacing between a power distribution simulation tool, OpenDSS, and a deep RL agent. The deep RL agent dynamically adjusts the capacitor bank operation through iterative learning to maintain bus voltages within predefined limits. Furthermore, the performance of the DDQN agent is compared with that of the DQN agent and the conventional capacitor controller embedded within OpenDSS.

articleTitle: Linear Modified Distribution Power Flow Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The distribution network (DN), generally radial in structure, is under focus due to the continuous increase in the addition of new components ranging from distributed energy resources (DERs) to electric vehicle charging stations (EVCSs). The latest addition will effectively increase the variation in DN states (bus voltage phasors) by continuously changing the bus injection values. Hence, power flow (PF) analysis is needed to obtain the values of DN states quickly. Another feature of DN is the inherent high R/X ratio of the associated lines. Thus, the conventional backward-forward sweep method has been used due to better suitability with radial DNs of high R/X ratio. For this, a modified distribution power flow (Mod-Dist-Flow) method has been derived in this paper, and its lossless model is tested on standard IEEE 33 bus and 69 bus balanced test systems. The results obtained compared with AC power flow (ACPF) and linear distribution (Lin-Dist-Flow) PF solution indicate a significant improvement of atleast 74.72% over Lin-Dist-Flow PF solution for the test cases. Bus voltage angle evaluation after attaining bus voltage magnitudes illustrates another advantage of the proposed Mod-Dist-Flow.

articleTitle: Minimisation of Neutral Current in Distribution Network by Home Level Rephasing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Unbalance is one of the biggest problems associated with a distribution system. It can lead to increased copper losses, thermal loading and neutral conductor size. This work proposes an algorithm to address the unbalance, hence reduce the neutral current of the system. The results obtained are reproducible. Consumers are classified into industrial, commercial, agricultural and residential. Phase allocation of single-phase residential consumers is changed to achieve overall system balance. Balancing was carried out initially at an intra-bus level starting from the end of the lateral feeders. Unbalance between phases is calculated for each time interval at each bus. Houses are identified to be rephased within the same bus. This method however addresses only the unbalance within individual buses. If any unbalance is not addressed within a bus, balancing is carried out in the previous bus such that the net unbalance of the considered buses is minimized. The results are demonstrated using the IEEE 33-bus system.

articleTitle: Distributed Economic Dispatch in a Microgrid Using Proportional-Integral Consensus
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: With the increasing penetration of distributed generators, distributed algorithms have become essential for efficient power system operations. However, these algorithms are often vulnerable to noise and communication delays due to their dependence on communication infrastructures. A consensus-based decentralized method is presented in this paper to solve economic dispatch in microgrids, accounting for practical communication challenges such as dynamically switching topologies, communication delays, and noise. A proportional-integral (PI) consensus protocol is proposed to address these issues, which includes an integral term to mitigate the harmful effects of noise and delays. The multi-agent system (MAS) model is used to describe the microgrid. A distributed PI consensus approach with two primary consensus variables—the global power imbalance (∆P ) and the incremental cost (λ)—is employed to solve the economic dispatch problem. A key benefit of this method is that it allows generating units to maintain the confidentiality of their cost characteristics. The effectiveness of the presented approach is demonstrated by simulation results on a microgrid with five buses.

articleTitle: Adapting Software-defined Information Centric Networks for IEC 61850-based Substations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: A robust communication infrastructure is the backbone of power system efficiency and reliability advancements, enabling real-time data exchange and control. The smart grid, a complex network of digital devices, relies on their seamless communication to share information for monitoring, control, and protection. As the number of these devices and their communication needs increase, the role of software-defined and information-centric networking frameworks will become more pronounced for offering reliable and secure operation solutions. Given the time-sensitive nature and specific architecture of smart grid protocols, software-defined information centric networks (SD-ICN) can be appropriately designed to meet these requirements. SD-ICN can improve security by controlling access and authentication and efficient distribution of contents in the network. This paper explores recent SD-ICN structures and strategies to improve the reliability and security of communication in power systems substations. An IEC 61850-based substation networking architecture is presented to demonstrate the application of SD-ICN. Additionally, a mechanism to map the substation devices using Substation Configuration Language (SCL) to a routable Named Data Networking (NDN) name to route in the SD-ICN network is proposed.

articleTitle: Optimal Placement of Distributed Energy Resources to Enhance Resilience in Electrical Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The resilience of electrical distribution systems (EDS) is critical for the continuity of essential services, particularly in the face of increasing natural disasters. While EDS reliability has been emphasized historically, resilience has recently gained attention due to its broader scope of maintaining system integrity during and after disturbances. This study proposes a novel optimization framework for the optimal placement of Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) in EDS, enhancing resilience, especially during extreme events. Leveraging a modified Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Optimization (MOPSO) algorithm, this research addresses the challenge of maintaining continuous power supply to critical loads. We use a new resilience metric aligned with the Resilience Analysis Process (RAP) from Sandia National Laboratories, accommodating the complex network topology and system variations. From the results, it is found that when contrasted with configurations optimized solely for power loss, the proposed approach demonstrates a slight increase in power loss of 1 kW but yields an improvement in resilience of 3.3%. This trade-off needs to be considered when incorporating resilience considerations into EDS planning.

articleTitle: Analysing the usage of carbon-intensive generation for balancing services in Great Britain and the potential impact of energy storage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Significant quantities of carbon-intensive generation are utilised yearly as part of Great Britain’s grid balancing. Alongside this, wind generation is regularly curtailed via the balancing mechanism. In order to reach net-zero targets, the grid balancing activities need to be decarbonised. This work presents a first-of-its-kind study into the feasibility of mitigating balancing mechanism activity on a site-by-site basis using energy storage. 17 combined-cycle gas turbines (CCGTs) and 12 wind generation sites are investigated to highlight their activity throughout 2023 identifying trends and potential opportunities for energy storage deployment. The paper finishes with a study of the sizing requirements to replace individual CCGTs on the balancing mechanism, showing that to displace 1.1TWh of carbon-intensive balancing mechanism activity a 26GWh energy storage system would be required.

articleTitle: Coordinating Numerical Relays with Voltage-Time-Current Characteristics in DG Integrated Power Networks and Implementation using FPGA
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: This paper presents the coordination of numerical relays having voltage-current-time characteristics in distributed generation (DG) connected power system networks. The nonstandard numerical relay settings are complex to formulate as the relay operating time equation is nonlinear with voltage and current variables. Hence, the coordination framework becomes a nonlinear constrained optimization problem. To solve this coordination problem, a new naturally inspired optimization algorithm named, the Chaotic Coyote Optimization Algorithm (CCOA) is employed. The coordination model is employed on the 8 bus system which is designed in DIGSILENT integrated with a 40 MW PV-DG. The numerical relay settings are validated from the fault data extracted from DIGSILENT in field-programmable gate array (FPGA) using MATLAB SIMULINK interface.

articleTitle: Plugging into Profit: An Economic Analysis of Electric Vehicle Participation in Frequency Regulation in India
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: To tackle climate change, there is a global effort to decarbonize different energy carriers, which includes electrification of the transportation sector. The increasing penetration of Electric Vehicle (EV) on roadways has led to extensive research and development around EVs. EVs, like most other personal vehicles, are typically parked for approximately 80% of their operational life, providing a significant opportunity to harness their batteries for essential grid support services, particularly frequency regulation (FR). This paper conducts a comprehensive profit analysis tailored to the city of New Delhi in India. Its objective is to elucidate the two-fold benefits of incorporating EVs for frequency regulation and establishing a revenue stream for individual EV owners. The study features the potential economic viability and technical advantages of integrating EVs into the broader energy landscape. The comprehensive analysis suggests a substantial profit for EV users. This substantial financial incentive encourages active participation in FR services, providing an economically viable strategy for the grid operator to address and mitigate frequency deviations.

articleTitle: Fault Analysis of Hybrid AC/DC Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The increasing integration of voltage source converters (VSCs) in the electric grid has significantly enhanced efficiency and reduced the carbon footprint of power networks. With the growing adoption of VSC, future networks are anticipated to be hybrid AC/DC systems. Analysis of these complex systems is critical for their planning, operation, and design. However, accurately simulating converters during symmetrical fault conditions in large hybrid AC/DC networks remains challenging due to the lack of comprehensive VSC models that account for AC and DC grid interactions. This paper tackles this issue by proposing a phase domain fault analysis method utilizing a quasi-static VSC model interface between the AC and DC grids. Verification studies conducted with PSCAD/EMTDC on the modified IEEE 30-bus network demonstrate the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed method for symmetrical faults.

articleTitle: The Development and Potential of Green Hydrogen in India
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The search for alternative fuel sources has been driven by the need for a sustainable energy future. Most current forms of energy produce vast amounts of carbon content and release it into the atmosphere. This has led to a global rise in temperature levels and is seen as the immediate threat faced by all humans. In a bid to tackle this, renewable energy and green hydrogen are seen as the leading solutions. As many countries, including India, have set goals for green hydrogen, we have conducted this study to identify what the scenario is in other countries, as well as what the scenario is in India. Our focus is on Green Hydrogen, the Hydrogen Economy, Climate Change, Production of Green Hydrogen, Hydrogen Storage, and Potential of Green Hydrogen in India.

articleTitle: Integration of Smart Grid Ready Heat Pumps in Home Energy Management Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: This work investigates the optimized operations of an air source heat pump (HP) system designed to maintain desired temperatures in a single-family house in London. The home is modeled using DesignBuilder and is configured for ASHRAE standards for indoor thermal comfort. The required heating capacity requirements are determined using EnergyPlus. Finally Smart Grid (SG) ready signals are leveraged to optimize the HP operation by dynamically adjusting settings based on peak and off-peak electricity rates as well as outdoor temperature. The energy performance of the home with HP always on and room temperature maintained at a constant is compared against the strategies which leverage low prices and outdoor temperatures. The strategies use the SG ready modes and lower the setpoint during specific periods. Results indicated significant reductions in energy consumption and costs, especially when heating is aligned with lower tariff periods. Additionally, the study explored the effects of weather conditions on heat pump efficiency, utilizing real-time and forecasted data for optimal performance adjustments. Overall, the findings demonstrate that integrating SG ready signals and adaptive temperature control can effectively maintain thermal comfort while minimizing energy consumption and costs. This approach offers a promising strategy for enhancing the efficiency and cost-effectiveness of residential heating systems in temperate climates.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Control Scheme for Voltage Regulation and Energy Loss Minimization in Active Distribution Networks Based on Model Predictive Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: This paper presents a real-time hybrid control scheme in active distribution networks for voltage regulation and energy loss minimization. The control model employs a model predictive control-based centralized controller at the upper layer to coordinate on-load tap changer, photovoltaic systems, and electric vehicle charging stations through a multi-time step optimization model. The centralized control involves a multi-time scale coordination, considering the varying temporal characteristics of control resources. At the lower layer, a rapid-response local control mechanism, operating within seconds is designed to address frequent voltage violations and act as a backup in case the centralized control system fails. The effectiveness of the proposed control strategy is validated on the 33-bus distribution network and the IEEE 123-bus distribution network.

articleTitle: Weather Impact on DER Long-term Performance: A Formal Verification Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Distributed energy resources (DERs), such as solar photovoltaic (PV) panels, are essential to modern energy systems, providing resilience and producing clean, local energy. However, their long-term performance is vulnerable to environmental factors, often leading to undetected issues due to the complexity of systematic monitoring. To address this, we propose a work-in-progress approach leveraging stochastic modeling to analyse and verify system requirements. This approach enables a rigorous evaluation of performance under varying weather conditions, as shown in our preliminary results, representing a significant step forward in managing renewable energy resources effectively.

articleTitle: A Fast Dynamic Internal Predictive Power Scheduling Approach for Power Management in Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: This paper presents a Dynamic Internal Predictive Power Scheduling (DIPPS) approach for optimizing power management in microgrids, particularly focusing on external power exchanges among diverse prosumers. DIPPS utilizes a dynamic objective function with a time-varying binary parameter to control the timing of power transfers to the external grid, facilitated by efficient usage of energy storage for surplus renewable power. The microgrid power scheduling problem is modeled as a mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP-PS) and subsequently transformed into a mixed-integer linear programming (MILPPS) optimization through McCormick’s relaxation to reduce computational complexity. A predictive window window with 6 data points is solved at an average of 0.92s, a 97.6% improvement over the 38.27s required for the MINLP-PS formulation, implying the numerical feasibility of the DIPPS approach for real-time implementation. Finally, the approach is validated against a static objective using real-world load data across three case studies with different time-varying parameters, demonstrating the ability of DIPPS to optimize power exchanges and efficiently utilize distributed resources while shifting the external power transfers to specified time durations.

articleTitle: Practical Evaluation of Existing Line Protection Methods for Networks Connected with Inverter-Based Renewable Sources: Wayforward
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Global renewable installed capacity is expected to increase by 75-90% replacing a major portion of the fossil fuel-based power plants by 2050 (as per forecasts by relevant agencies such as IEA and IRENA). Climate goals, energy security, economy are the major root causes of the shift. Renewable sources are connected to the grid through power electronic converters, unlike conventional sources. The influence of these power electronics converters poses challenges to line protection methodologies. This is due to their unique fault response characterized by limited and control-modulated fault currents. Fault response could also vary from grid to grid depending on prevailing grid codes related to renewable integration. The protection methodologies developed decades back and were created using knowledge of traditional power systems are now at risk of failing. Many practical relay failure cases have been reported due to renewable integration in our discussions with various utilities. In this paper, we evaluate the existing line protection methodologies for lines connected with renewables using experimental and field data. The major challenges and findings are presented in the paper and a way forward is also recommended for further scope of research in this domain.

articleTitle: Resilience Evaluation of Electrical Distribution Systems with DER and EVCI
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Resilience has recently gained interest in all areas of engineering with the goal of developing resilient operational systems that can handle any threat or event. The better half of the last decade has given rise to several research and evaluation standards to define resilience in electrical distribution systems (EDS). Many researchers have proposed various metrics for the evaluation of resilience, considering different parameters. However, a comprehensive metric that is consistent for various changes in the system configuration and different practical scenarios is still being searched. We propose a metric that considers the system’s inherent properties along with service-based parameters considering service possibilities and service fulfilment conditions. The performance evaluation of the proposed metric is analyzed for varied cases of integration of distributed energy sources (DERs) and critical loads (CLs). Also, we have considered a scenario that takes into account the electrical vehicle charging infrastructures (EVCI) as CLs, which will soon be a near-futuristic scenario where energy vehicles (EVs) need to be charged at the charging stations to provide services during extreme events. The resilience of the system increases from 82% to 97% with the inclusion of DERs and drops by less than 1% with the addition of more CLs and EVCIs. The proposed metric demonstrated consistency in the resilience evaluation across a wide range of cases and is robust and suitable for the EDS’s goals for planning and operational resilience.

articleTitle: Battery Health Prediction Using Commixtured Multi-Feature Selection and Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The data-driven methods have their limitations such as data-insufficiency and data-discrepancy when deployed in real-onboard applications for highly complex and non-linear applications like lithium-ion battery (LIB) health prognosis. Moreover, the accuracy and robustness of the health prediction depends largely on the feature selection for the machine learning (ML) model. To address these shortcomings, this paper proposes a CNN-FiWr-BiLSTM based state of health (SoH) prediction model that uses Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to automatically extract features from the battery data while a commixture of filter and wrapper methods (FiWr) eliminates both irrelevant and redundant features to obtain more effective feature set. The bi-directional long short term memory (BiLSTM) network learns the ageing features of LIB over time and finally, the SoH regression prediction is made by fully-connected (FC) layer. Furthermore, considering different degradation trajectories exhibited by the dynamic operating conditions, this paper introduces transfer learning (TL) to improve the generalizability and the prediction performance of the model. With experimental validation across the lifetime data of 08 batteries aged cyclically under variable drive profiles, the proposed framework shows overwhelming effectiveness as compared to CNN and BiLSTM alone with root mean square error (RMSE) of less than 0.14% and maximum absolute error (MAE) of less than 02.99 for all batteries.

articleTitle: A Transactive Energy Framework for Real-Time Primary Frequency Support by Active Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Modern active distribution networks possess significant potential to deliver ancillary services to transmission networks owing to the rising integration of renewable energy sources. This study explores the provision of primary frequency support from active distribution network to transmission network via price-based transactive control of microgrid inverters. The proposed method aims to achieve efficient coordination among microgrids, optimizing their utility, while also assisting the active distribution network in optimal primary frequency support provision to transmission network. The feasibility of this approach for real-time application is validated using a real-time simulator.

articleTitle: Computing Feasible Operating Region: A Polytope-based Approach for Aggregator-DNO Coordination
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Distribution network operators (DNOs) are grappling with numerous challenges due to integration and expansion of distributed energy resources (DERs) in the distribution network (DN). These DERs have the potential to offer control and flexibility assistance to the DNO if exploited judiciously. However, the management of these DERs can be challenging for the DNO. An aggregator, serving as a bridge between DERs and DNO, could assist the DNO in avoiding network constraint violations while reducing the dimensionality. Therefore, this paper proposes an aggregator-DNO coordination model by computing feasible operating regions for DERs via a box polytope/hyper-rectangle-based geometric approach. Aggregators form their bids by aggregating the DER's feasible operating regions via the Minkowski sum. Considering these aggregated bids, the DNO runs a network-constrained optimization model and sends disaggregation signals to the aggregators. It also conveys the feasible operating DER regions for optimal deployment by the aggregator, adhering to network constraints. Hence, the proposed geometric approach holds significant potential for an efficient and effective management of DERs while respecting network feasibility.

articleTitle: Evaluating wall installation methods for cylindrical solar cells in urban areas by luminous flux simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: In urban areas of Japan, such as Tokyo, overcrowding in condominiums and office buildings leaves limited flat land for installing solar panels, resulting in inadequate installation of renewable energy. To advance photovoltaic power generation and support Japan's goal of achieving carbon neutrality by 2050, we are exploring the use of cylindrical solar cells in these dense urban settings. Cylindrical solar cells are ideal for metropolitan installations due to their lightweight design and wind resistance. However, it is crucial to consider how installation configurations influence electricity production, especially the need to minimize shadowing from nearby buildings and other urban elements. This study utilized lighting simulation software to model the light flux based on actual installation conditions of cylindrical solar cells to identify optimal placement strategies. Additionally, this configuration was compared with traditional flat-plate solar cells under similar conditions. Findings indicate that cylindrical solar cells offer flexible installation options. Notably, employing a horizontal grid layout for cylindrical cells addresses the challenges associated with wall-mounted flat-plate cells, which suffer reduced luminous flux at higher solar altitudes. These results demonstrate that cylindrical solar cells can effectively overcome the challenges of photovoltaic installation in densely populated urban areas.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Fault Detection Methods in Electrical Power Systems Using Hessian Locally Linear Embedding and Deep Autoencoders
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Faults in power lines greatly impact the reliability of electrical distribution systems (EDS), causing instability and heightened risks of outages. Accurate detection of electrical faults is required for optimizing the operation and maintenance of the power system. In this paper, we conduct a comparative study of two advanced approaches for detecting faults in EDS: Hessian locally linear embedding (HLLE) and convolutional autoencoders (CAE). The first approach utilizes HLLE to convert data with high dimensionality into low dimensionality embedding coordinates. This process helps capture underlying variations and patterns, enabling robust feature extraction. The detection of faults is achieved by applying the Mann-Whitney U test. The second approach leverages deep learning techniques, specifically deep autoencoders for anomaly-based fault detection and CAEs for dimensionality reduction. Deep autoencoders offer powerful capabilities in pattern classification, while CAEs require less training time due to fewer parameters. Simulations conducted on an electrical distribution system showcase the effectiveness of both approaches. However, the deep autoencoder approach outperforms the HLLE-based method, achieving an accuracy of 97% on simulated datasets. This comparative study provides valuable insights into the developments of robust detection systems in EDS.

articleTitle: Damage-Based Stochastic Restoration Against Wind-Induced Events for a Resilient Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Rapid increase in weather events suggests the need for an approach to capture and quantify the damage intensity of uncertain events. This paper develops a tool that formulates the problem as a two-stage approach against uncertain wind events. The first stage investigates the dynamic wind impact on vulnerable overhead components and models the component-level fragility curve. This approach overpowers the past fragility modeling by framing a hybrid dataset for a realistic weather-dependent analysis. The second stage formulates the problem mathematically using the markov decision process, where the state transition is illustrated via a directed graph, exhibiting five stages: normal, failure, retrofit, replace, and restore. It depicts the statistically estimated action and optimizes the cost as a reward. The novel event-driven dynamic programming algorithm is devised to minimize the expected cost by deriving an optimal policy for each state-based action. The formulated damage-level assessment matrix evaluates the real-time damage status and suggests a relevant remedial measure. The proposed approach is implemented on modified IEEE 33 bus system with an extensive case study, delivering optimal results for a resilient and cost-effective power distribution system.

articleTitle: Adaptive Power Management of Large-Scale Electric Vehicle Charging Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Demand for public charging is growing with the increasing adoption of electric vehicles (EV). Motivated by these developments, the parking industry is fast transitioning from pure play parking to parking with charging; but are facing difficulties to scale charging operations due to high infrastructure costs and grid-level capacity constraints. These challenges can be potentially alleviated by organizing the charging network into clusters, each consisting of a collection of EV chargers. To prevent imbalances between the charging demand across network clusters and available power supply, while being able to service different type of customers with priority for prime users; the power flow in the charging network needs to be managed intelligently. To achieve this, we consider the problem of optimal power allocation to not only satisfy these multiple system objectives, but also scale efficiently to large network sizes involving hundreds of clusters and charging points. We present a solution approach based on mixed-integer linear program (MILP) to overcome the above challenges. Using simulations, we show that MILP performs better than a greedy approach by allocating 12% more power to prime customers while respecting various system constraints; with solution speed ranging from a few seconds (on small networks) to less than a minute (on large networks).

articleTitle: Federated Learning for Residential Load and PV Production Forecast
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: This paper explores the application of federated learning in predicting energy consumption and solar production for households equipped with Enphase smart home solar systems.
