Traditional centralized model training for energy prediction entails significant communication overhead, particularly when dealing with distributed data sources. To mitigate this challenge, federated learning is proposed as a privacy-preserving alternative, wherein each client trains a local model on its data and transmits model updates to a central server for aggregation. We propose a neural network-based energy demand predictor trained with federated learning, leveraging distributed data while maintaining prediction accuracies. Federated learning ensures data security and confidentiality by transmitting only model updates, preserving individual privacy. The datasets used are anonymized, and the actual data cannot be extracted from the shared gradients. Through experiments, we demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of federated learning in energy forecasting, highlighting its potential to enhance prediction capabilities without compromising privacy.

articleTitle: Exploring the Efficacy of Feature Selection and Attention Enhanced Deep Learning in Multivariable Electricity Price Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Accurate electricity price prediction has become critical for operational decision making and strategy making. In recent years, machine learning techniques have emerged as an effective solution for the day ahead electricity market price forecasting problem. However, despite their capability to make accurate predictions, they lack transparency and often leave the researchers with a non-understandable black box impression. Electricity prices present dependance on several external factors, and deep learning techniques, with their inherent capabilities to deal with temporal dependencies and non-linearity, offer solutions to these multivariable dependent forecasting problems. This paper explores the efficacy of integrating advanced feature selection techniques and attention-enhanced deep learning models in multivariable electricity price forecasting.A robust methodology, combining Pearson correlation matrix-based feature selection Stacked Long-Short Term Memory (SLSTM) network followed by an attention mechanism, has been proposed to make the process more transparent. This study validates the efficacy of proposed methodology on real world electricity market dataset of Sweden. This comprehensive dataset encompasses multiple variables influencing electricity prices, s.a. electrical demand and weather data. The study further compares two scenarios, one inclusive of all the features and the other with selective features and attention-based approach. The results underscore the importance of effective feature selection and the incorporation of attention mechanism in enhancing the predictive capabilities of deep learning models for electricity price forecasting. The proposed methodology not only generates more accurate forecasts than the base case but also results in a reduction in computational time.

articleTitle: Development and Parameter Extraction of Simplified Empirical Polarization Curve Model for Polymer Electrolyte Membrane Fuel Cell
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Fuel cells play a significant role in the domain of sustainable development due to their high efficiency and low environmental impacts. Polymer Electrolyte Membrane Fuel Cells (PEMFC) are particularly promising alternatives for their transportation and stationary power generation applications. Accurate modeling of PEMFCs is vital for achieving optimal performance, which is generally evaluated using polarization curves. In this study, a simplified empirical polarization curve model for PEMFCs is developed. Experimental data is collected using the Nexa 1200 PEMFC test system. The model parameters are derived through a non-linear FMINCON optimization process and the model is validated across multiple polarization datasets. The results show a low Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and a close match between the experimental stack voltage and the modeled stack voltage, indicating a good agreement with the model. Additionally, the variation of polarization losses (activation, ohmic, and concentration) with stack current is analyzed, demonstrating the robustness of the model and its potential for accurately predicting PEMFC performance, under different operating conditions.

articleTitle: Substation Vulnerability Assessment Using Bayesian Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Security of substations is important to ensure reliability and integrity of the power grid. In this paper, we provide a complete vulnerability assessment framework for a SAS substation. The framework uses CVE database as its foundation. We use an NLP-based model to identify and map the vulnerabilities present in each CVE entry. These mapped vulnerabilities are then used to determine various attack paths in a test network using Bayesian networks. We also compute the exploitation probabilities of the vulnerability nodes and the attack paths in the network. Our study provides an overall vulnerability landscape of the network which can be used to identify weak points and implement remedial security measures to fix them.

articleTitle: Demand Response Platform with IoT and NILM for Household Energy Management
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Effective and proactive energy management is crucial in the modern economy. Demand Response (DR) serves as a key strategy for optimizing electricity supply per consumer needs. This paper presents an Internet of Things-based system designed to manage DR through the scheduling of household appliances. By leveraging Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring (NILM) techniques, the system is capable of identifying and controlling individual electrical loads. Users can input their preferences via a local host interface, enabling the system to control appliance schedules and reduce overall power consumption. The methodology for real-time monitoring and calculation of energy usage is discussed, facilitating accurate predictions of electricity costs based on regional tariffs. The present investigative approach not only enhances energy efficiency but also offers consumers greater control over electricity billing. The paper aims to demonstrate the practical application of IoT and NILM in creating smarter, more responsive energy management solutions.

articleTitle: Stress Impacts on Turbo-generator Shaft in Inverter- Dominated Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The large-scale integration of renewable energy (RE) in form of inverter-based resources (IBRs) have posed concerns on required level of rotational inertia in power systems. Gradual decrease of rotational inertia, intermittent nature of renewables and frequency instability issues have raised the occurrence and severity of the rate of change of frequency (RoCoF) events in power system. Design considerations of grid-connected synchronous generators are not adhered to severe RoCoF, thereby leading to mechanical stress on turbine shafts. Impact analysis of this kind is of potential use to generation utility owners and transmission system operators for planning utility activities and reliability. This study investigates the impact of IBRs on a turbo-generator (TG) shaft in modified IEEE-14 bus system. Utilizing a 300 MVA synchronous machine with TGOV4 governing model as a case study, torques induced by varying active power in steps were analyzed and applied to a multi-mass model. The resulting torques were then subjected to structural analysis to identify structural deformations. The findings highlight considerable stress impacts on high-pressure turbine shaft, emphasizing the challenges for turbo-generators in IBR dominated power grids.

articleTitle: Optimal Allocation of Multiple Distributed Generation Using an Enhanced Whale Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The integration of distributed generation (DG) into the distribution system is a complex problem that requires an efficient optimization technique. To maximize benefits while minimizing disadvantages, it is crucial to determine optimal locations and capacities for DG installations. Despite the frequent use of recently developed optimization algorithms, their enhanced counterparts are rarely investigated. Moreover, most research relied on peak loads, which do not accurately reflect real-world demand. We proposed using the enhanced whale optimization algorithm (E-WOA) for optimal DG allocation in a radial distribution system, aiming to minimize power and energy losses. This study also developed representative variable load profiles based on real-world consumption data. The backward/forward sweep algorithm is used for load flow analysis, with the IEEE 33-Bus radial distribution system serving as the test system. The optimization was simulated over 100 independent runs, each with 200 iterations and a population of 50. Results demonstrated that E-WOA effectively solves the optimal DG allocation problem, achieving a power loss of 72.785 kW for three DGs at unity power factor, outperforming the standard WOA and several recent algorithms, and matching the performance of hybrid algorithms. Comparison with WOA across different loading scenarios showed that E-WOA consistently produced higher quality solutions at the cost of slower convergence speeds, longer runtimes, and poor scalability. These suggest E-WOA’s limitations in addressing large-scale optimization tasks.

articleTitle: A Novel Fault Severity Factor based Protection Strategy for the Inverter-based Distribution Networks Considering System Strength
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The Point of Common Coupling (PCC) serves as a hub for connecting various Inverter-Based Resources (IBRs), interconnected network grid, and loads. Designing a protection strategy for the faults that occur near the PCC is critical for the sake of maintaining connections of IBRs as per grid codes and preventing the system from the verge of transient instability. In contrast to existing methods, the proposed protection strategy offers a pragmatic approach to determine the fault severity. It considers not only faulty conditions but also pre-fault states, providing a holistic view of system dynamics. Additionally, it introduces self-tuned relay protection characteristics that dynamically adjust sensitivity and selectivity, considering standard voltage tolerance levels and changes in the system strength. Moreover, the suggested strategy integrates low voltage ride-through limits of connected IBRs in the protection characteristics, facilitating fault clearance without unduly disconnection of IBRs. Through detailed modeling and IBR controls simulated on the Matlab platform, efficacy of the proposed strategy is demonstrated across various pre-fault and faulty conditions, showcasing its adaptability and secure protective relaying performance.

articleTitle: Process Bus Design and Implementation Aspects for a Digital Substation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: This paper describes the important design aspects for implementing an alternate solution called process bus in digital substations, replacing the traditional hardwired solutions utilizing integrated multi-function relays. IEC 61850-9-2 is a globally accepted standard for process bus solutions. However, its adoption by utilities has been gaining momentum in recent days after the implementation of the IEC 61850-based substation automation system at the station level, which offers various advantages of standardization and interoperability, including in India. It is important to understand the latest design aspects in IEDs related to the process bus to emphasize the various benefits of implementing such solutions. Process bus relates to the engineering, construction, commissioning, and routine maintenance for transitioning from traditional Protection and Control (P&C) based systems to modern systems. Although the benefits of deploying practical IEC 61850 process bus-based P&C systems are majorly accounted for as cost savings and reduced labour costs, particularly in greenfield installations, not all benefits can be understood as only specific monetary savings. Several advantages relate to the ability to better optimize the utilization and deployment of substation resources, improving the overall efficiency in using the substation equipment’s data and improving operations with increased situational awareness. This paper presents evidence of how process bus design, related architecture and features can provide several advantages in substation modernization and operation for widespread adoption in the Indian power sector.
